audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Xerath / Xerath / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill while the content layer and the packet chart both read Xerath five times then Azir twice. Five rows rendered two different answers.
audit.why: Win rate is 44.32% over 837 games and the shape is not in dispute: Xerath owns levels 1-6 on Eye of Destruction at 1000 and Shocking Orb at 1050 against a soldier that reaches roughly 875, and Azir takes the game back once Nashor's lands and a 1100-range Shifting Sands can put him on top of a champion with no dash.
audit.corrected: full phases[2..4].side moved Skill->Xerath and phases[5..6].side moved Skill->Azir, each with its why rewritten in the same proposal. content win[] already matched the packet and was left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike named Rite of the Arcane but carried no cooldown or range, and the late spike claimed Azir wins fights without saying why.
audit.why: Rite of the Arcane is 130/115/100s at 5000 range and Riot's text says Xerath immobilizes himself for it. Emperor's Divide is 120/105/90s. Nashor's plus a 1100-range Shifting Sands is the actual mechanism by which Azir reaches him.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns and ranges written into spikes[1], spikes[3], breakdown.mid, content mid and content late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability errors and one false mechanic. The page called the stun 'Eye of Destruction (E)' in spikes[0], early and wants.foe[1] — Eye of Destruction is W and does not stun; the stun is Shocking Orb (E). And wants.you[1] and early told the player to hide behind minions, which does not work against Arcanopulse.
audit.why: Kit file: W Eye of Destruction, 14/13/12/11/10s at 1000, slow and zone only. E Shocking Orb, 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s at 1050, hardCC. Q Arcanopulse 'deals magic damage to all targets hit' — it pierces the wave, so minions are not cover from it. Rite of the Arcane carries both the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it') and Riot's own 'Xerath immobilizes himself', so Emperor's Divide's knockback ends the barrage.
audit.corrected: Names fixed everywhere. The pierce written into breakdown.early, report[5].t, content early, loading and wants.you[1]. The R interrupt written into phases[6].why, whys[6], spikes[3], breakdown.late, content mid, content late and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit — defect catalogue item 3. dosFull[2].d also quoted a 'fifteen-second invitation' for Shocking Orb, and dontsFull[1].d a nineteen-second Shifting Sands.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 falling to 11s at rank 5, not 15. Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1; 19s is rank 3.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with Shocking Orb 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s at 1050, Eye of Destruction 14s at rank 1, Shifting Sands 22s at rank 1 and Rite of the Arcane 130s at rank 1. dosFull[2].d repurposed to match its own title with Arcanopulse's 80-120 mana cost and Mana Surge. dontsFull[1].d corrected to 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed on dosFull[1].d (tradeGood verbatim) and dontsFull[2].d (tradeBad verbatim); dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d explained something other than their titles; and tradeBad asserted 'the engage window every Xerath player is waiting for' when Xerath has no engage at all.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 2, plus a factual inversion — an artillery mage with no dash is not waiting for an engage window.
audit.corrected: All five bodies rewritten against their own titles using Xerath's real ranges and cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave recommended a controlled slow push, which is the worst possible wave state against artillery.
audit.why: A slow push means standing in one place in a lane where Shocking Orb reaches 1050 and Arcanopulse pierces everything between you.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around holding the wave near your tower and crashing on the Eye of Destruction cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr, enemyWin, ahead, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding and breakdown.late were name-swap templates, and tldr's 'soldier range vs spell range' claimed a range advantage Azir does not have here.
audit.why: Template sweep plus a factual inversion — Xerath out-ranges Azir, which is the entire premise of the matchup.
audit.corrected: Each regrounded on survive-then-close: he out-ranges you and cannot move, so the win condition is reaching Nashor's and then reaching him.

edits.before: Xerath is one of the most oppressive ranged poke matchups you'll face — his Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction both outrange your soldiers, so he can chip your health bar every wave with almost no risk of retaliation. edits.after: Xerath is one of the most oppressive ranged poke matchups you'll face — Eye of Destruction (W) at 1000 and Shocking Orb (E) at 1050 both reach past your soldiers, so he chips your health bar every wave with almost no risk. Arcanopulse pierces the whole wave, so minions are not cover from it; sidestep instead, and never step forward with your Shifting Sands down.

edits.before: Level 6 is genuinely his strongest window — Rite of the Arcane adds even more poke and siege potential, making this the hardest stretch of the lane to survive. edits.after: Level 6 is genuinely his strongest window — Rite of the Arcane is 130s at rank 1 and fires from 5000 units, making this the hardest stretch of the lane to survive. Stay topped off and manage the wave rather than contesting him directly; the moment he starts channelling it inside your reach, Emperor's Divide ends the barrage.

edits.before: Full build Azir can finally punish Xerath's stationary poke pattern — your soldier mobility and ultimate let you close distance and force him into uncomfortable positions in skirmishes, while his kit has no answer for sustained pressure up close. edits.after: Full build you finally punish his stationary pattern — Shifting Sands covers 1100 onto a soldier and Xerath has no dash to answer it, so once you are on top of him his kit does nothing. Rite of the Arcane immobilizes him for the whole channel: Emperor's Divide knocks him out of it mid-barrage. Play around vision in neutral moments; once fights start you are the threat.

notes: Two real ability errors fixed: the page called Xerath's stun 'Eye of Destruction (E)' in spikes[0], content early and wants.foe[1]. Eye of Destruction is W (slow/zone, 14s, 1000 range); the stun is Shocking Orb (E) (13/12.5/12/11.5/11s, 1050 range). The packet's suspectNames entry on wants.foe[1] was correct. Also removed the 'use minions to block skillshots' advice — Arcanopulse 'deals magic damage to all targets hit' and pierces the wave, so minions are not cover from it. I did NOT assert that minions or Sand Soldiers block Shocking Orb: the projectile flag is derived and Riot's text for E says only 'Deals magic damage to an enemy and stuns them', so the blocking behaviour is unknown from the data I have. Chart resolved as one unit: full phases[2..4].side Skill->Xerath and phases[5..6].side Skill->Azir, whys rewritten with each. Ratings left untouched — their polarity is ambiguous across this repo and I did not want to guess it across five rows. I have written that Emperor's Divide knocks Xerath out of Rite of the Arcane; this rests on the kit's channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it') combined with Riot's own 'Xerath immobilizes himself'. It is the highest-value line in the matchup and I flagged it in unverified so it can be spot-checked before it ships.
